1.26.0: Seating: a new tab on each class. Pick how the room is set up, drag students to desks, and Shuffle gives everyone a new seat. A student can be kept in their seat.
Pick a name shows one student at random, and nobody twice until everyone has had a turn. Make groups deals the class into groups of any size.
While presenting a lesson, P picks a name and G makes groups. Who’s here leaves out anyone who is away today.
1.25.0: Attendance. Each class has an Attendance tab: everyone starts as present, so a day is one press for each student who is late, excused or absent, with a note if you want one.
Look back shows every saved day in one table with each student’s totals, and a student’s own page lists the days they missed.
Copy a day, or download the table as a spreadsheet, for your school’s system. Today has a line for it under each class.
If you don’t take attendance here, turn it off in Settings, Classes and rosters.
1.24.0: Retakes: a second try at the same assignment keeps the first try's score, comment and paper. Start one from the ⋯ beside Missing, Excused and Late on a paper.
You choose which try counts, for all your classes: the highest (to begin with), the latest, or the average. It is in the retake box and in the gradebook's Term setup.
A score typed into the gradebook takes a retake too: type both, like 7 > 10.
1.23.0: Scores by learning goal, if you want them. Keep your own list of goals (a skill, or a standard from your school) in Settings, Grading, or add one wherever you tag.
Tag rubric rows in Rubric setup and quiz questions in Quiz boxes. An assignment scored with just a total can carry one goal for the whole score.

Each class page gets a Goals tab: the class average on each goal with the lowest first, every student by every goal, and where each number came from. A student's own page shows their goals beside the class average.
Nothing changes until you add a first goal, and tagging never changes a score or a grade.
1.22.0: Progress sheets for parent meetings: one printed page per student with the term grade, every score, a chart of how they moved, missing work, each term's grade, the report comment and lines for notes. Find it on a class's Students list, or Progress sheet on one student's page.
Choose the term and tick what goes on it; Print opens the print window, where you can pick a printer or Save as PDF. It is made on your computer and nothing is sent anywhere.
1.21.0: Each class has a Missing work tab: every paper you marked Missing, by student or by assignment, for the term you pick.

Email reminder opens an email in your own mail app, addressed to the student and listing what they owe, for you to read and send. Email all writes one email to everyone who owes an assignment, with the addresses in Bcc. Grading Studio sends nothing itself.
Each reminder you open is noted beside the work, and Email wording… changes what every reminder says.
1.20.0: The app can speak Traditional Chinese (繁體中文). Choose it in Settings, Display, App language, or at the top of the welcome.

Like Spanish, it covers the first screens so far: the sidebar, Today, the welcome, Find anything, Help, and the feedback page students get with a returned paper. The other screens are still in English.
1.19.0: The app can speak Spanish. Choose it in Settings, Display, App language, or at the top of the welcome.
Spanish covers the first screens so far: the sidebar, Today, the welcome, Find anything, Help, and the feedback page students get with a returned paper. The other screens are still in English.
Names you typed (classes, students, assignments, rubric rows) are never translated.
1.18.0: On a tablet, a pencil draws and the pen's line is wider where you press harder. Once you have used a pencil, one finger moves the page, two fingers pinch to zoom, and a hand resting on the screen does nothing.
Settings, Marking has a new Tablet and pencil section: choose what a finger does on the paper, or turn off the wider line.
On a touch screen the tools, the student rows and the score buttons are larger.
1.17.0: Report comments: a new tab on each class's page drafts a comment for every student from your own gradebook, rubric scores and the comments you wrote on their papers. Edit each one, tick it done, then copy or download them all.
The drafts are put together on your computer from sentences you can change under Wording. Nothing about a student is sent anywhere.
1.16.0: Help is in the sidebar: short answers to the questions teachers ask most, from opening a set of papers to moving your work to another computer.
Find anything answers questions too. Type a few words, like “late paper” or “backup”, and the answer is in the list.
1.15.0: A picture dragged onto a slide that has text now sits beside the text, in a new Text + picture layout.
Drag several pictures in at once and each gets its own slide. Let a picture go on any slide in the list on the left to put it there.
New Full picture layout: the picture fills the whole slide.
1.14.0: Extra credit: points or a percent on one paper, and extra credit entries in the gradebook that add to the term grade or the in-class average.

The gradebook shows each type's average (summative, in-class) right beside the term grade, kept in view as you scroll. Averages only shows just those columns, and Whole year splits each term the same way.
Leave out… lets you untick students to see the class averages without them. Their own grades don't change, and nothing is saved.
1.13.0: Present a lesson from the Planner, or from Today when its class is on now or next: its slides fill the screen, and the arrow keys or a clicker move through them.
While presenting, A shows the agenda to tick off, T starts a timer the class can see, N shows your notes and B blanks the screen.
The bar shows how many minutes the class has left, from your timetable.
After a lesson is taught, one line says where the class got to. It shows on the lesson and on the week, and presenting again picks up there.
1.12.0: A returned paper starts with a feedback page: the score, each rubric row with the level given and what that level means, your comment, and every comment on the paper with its page number.
It is on unless you turn it off under Options on the Return tab. Your own pages are not changed, and bringing an export back in opens only those.
1.11.0: The Planner’s sections are in the sidebar: Calendar, Units, Past lessons, Activities and Rubrics. The row of tabs across the top is gone.
A lesson has a lighter top: its name, its classes, its status and Download. Copy for Claude, Versions, the upload and the links are under More.
Comments shows above a lesson once it has one.
1.7.0: Home is now Today: the classes you teach today with the lesson planned for each, the papers waiting to be marked, and the papers ready to hand back.
What the class needs next: after a set of papers is scored, Today shows the weakest rubric row and how many students to sit down with.
A class page is quieter. Click anywhere on an assignment’s row to open it; the only blue button is the one that adds an assignment.
Forget, and the other ways to open papers, moved into the ⋯ menu on each row.
1.6.0: A new browser opens on three questions (your classes, how you grade, where work is kept) and starts with nothing of anyone else’s in it.
A sample class of made-up students, with papers to mark, for trying things out. Remove it from Home when you’re done.
The app uses the name of your own school system. Choose it, and how you usually grade, in Settings.
Letter grades or IB 1 to 7 can show beside the percent, with boundaries you set.
Canvas and Moodle downloads are grouped by student. The Planner works without a setup file, and downloads lessons as PowerPoint with a plain built-in template.
1.5.0: The sidebar says “Not backed up”, in amber, until a folder holds a second copy of your work. Home asks for that folder once.
Go back in time, in Settings: any assignment as it was on an earlier day, restored on its own, with Undo.
Grading Studio can be installed as an app, and it opens with no internet.
A newer version now waits until you click Update now, so nothing changes in the middle of marking.
